item.title: Solving the World’s Microplastics Problem: 4 Solutions Cities and States are Trying After Global Treaty Talks Collapsed - The Planetary Press
item.description: Microplastics seem to be everywhere – in the air we breathe, the water we drink, the food we eat. They have turned up in human organs, blood, testicles, placentas and even brains. While the full health consequences of that exposure are not yet known, researchers are exploring potential links between microplastics and negative health effects such as male infertility, inflammation, liver disease and other metabolic problems, and heart attack or stroke.

item.title: How the Midnight Sun is Helping Displace Fossil Fuels in a Remote Arctic Community - The Planetary Press
item.description: For the past decade, the midnight sun has been helping the remote community of Colville Lake in the Canadian Arctic decrease its dependence on fossil fuels.

item.title: How this Swedish Tech Company is Protecting Nature in Cities - The Planetary Press
item.description: Nature surrounds us and is the foundation of everything we depend on: clean air, water, food, raw materials and a stable climate. Healthy ecosystems regulate temperatures, protect against extreme weather and pollinate crops.

item.title: Climate Solutions Can Start at Your Desk - The Planetary Press
item.description: Lucy Piper is with the nonprofit Work for Climate, which aims to change that. The group runs a three-month course, which teaches people how to push for climate action from within a company.

item.title: How AI-powered Citizen Science is Amplifying Community-led Climate Action - The Planetary Press
item.description: The rapid acceleration of climate change warrants more than just top-down solutions and expert interventions – it requires communities at the forefront to be equipped with cutting-edge technologies coupled with actionable insights and collaborative tools.

item.title: ‘Only If We Help Shall All Be Saved’: Jane Goodall Showed We Can All Be Part of the Solution - The Planetary Press
item.description: With the passing of Dr Jane Goodall, the world has lost a conservation giant. But her extraordinary achievements leave a profound legacy. Goodall was a world-leading expert in animal behaviour and a globally recognised environmental and conservation advocate. She achieved all this at a time when women were commonly sidelined or ignored in science.

item.title: How One Rancher Beat Drought, Debt, and Low Cotton Prices - The Planetary Press
item.description: The sheep graze around the solar panels, keeping weeds from shading them. And the farmers can still harvest meat, milk, and wool.

item.title: Growing a Mix of Plants in Fields Can Save Farmers Money and Help the Environment – New Research - The Planetary Press
item.description: Farmers have increasingly sown a single type of grass in their fields over the past 100 years, and then added chemical fertiliser to increase their harvest. But new research suggests that there are alternatives that are cheaper and can increase the potential of these grasslands to feed livestock.

item.title: How Healthy Soil and Land Creates Solid Ground for Global Resilience - The Planetary Press
item.description: Beneath every field, forest and city lies the quiet infrastructure of life. Soil is the foundation for the food we eat, the raw materials that power our industries and the natural cycles that sustain life on Earth.

item.title: Safeguarding the Australia's Iconic Koala: NSW Government Unveils Plans for Landmark Conservation Reserve - The Planetary Press
item.description: Few animals tug at Australian hearts like the koala. Yet the marsupial, once common along the eastern seaboard, was declared endangered in New South Wales (NSW) in 2022. Habitat loss, climate stress, and disease have driven populations down so far that a parliamentary inquiry warned they could vanish from the state before 2050. The proposed remedy is ambitious: the Great Koala National Park (GKNP), a 475,000-hectare protected area stretching from Kempsey to Grafton and inland to Ebor.
